subject: general
question:
How many water and carbon dioxide molecules take part, respectively, in the process of photosynthesis as indicated by the following unbalanced equation?

H₂O(l) + CO₂(g) → C₆H₁₂0₆(aq) + O₂(g) + H₂O(l) (In the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll).
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3: 6 and 6**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the process of photosynthesis, 6 molecules of water (H₂O) and 6 molecules of carbon dioxide (CO₂) are required to produce one molecule of glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆).
 
• The balanced chemical equation for photosynthesis is: **6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂** (in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll).
 
• Photosynthesis is a crucial biological process in which green plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy.
 
• Glucose synthesized during photosynthesis serves as a vital energy source for plants and other organisms.
 
• Oxygen is released as a byproduct during photosynthesis, which is essential for the survival of aerobic organisms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Definition of Photosynthesis:**

 
 
• Photosynthesis is the process by which plants use sunlight to synthesize nutrients from carbon dioxide and water.
 
• This process typically occurs in the chloroplasts of plant cells, which contain the pigment chlorophyll.
 
 
 
• **Role of Chlorophyll:**
 
 
• Chlorophyll is the green pigment in plants responsible for capturing light energy.
 
• It absorbs light mainly in the blue and red wavelengths, enabling the photosynthetic process.
 
 
 
• **Products of Photosynthesis:**
 
 
• The primary product is glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆), which is stored as starch in plants.
 
• Oxygen (O₂) is a secondary product released into the atmosphere, supporting life on Earth.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Photosynthesis:**
 
 
• It serves as the foundation of the food chain by providing energy-rich organic compounds.
 
• Photosynthesis helps regulate atmospheric CO₂ levels and contributes to oxygen production.
